title: Which short daily exercises sharpen your thinking and voice for case interviews?
description: Ten short daily exercises for case interview prep: recaps, speed maths, articulation, pacing, pauses and staying calm.
hook: Here are ten short exercises for your thinking, voice and nerves. Pick two or three and do them most days.
body:
Dual n-back (thinking)

Any dual n-back app. Start at 2-back; move up only above 80% accuracy.

How much: 10 min daily. What it trains: Holding several things in your head at once. Evidence that it improves interview performance is limited, so treat it as optional.

60-second recap (thinking)

Play 2 minutes of a business podcast, pause, recap it aloud in 60 seconds: 'three things were said…'

How much: 3-5 reps. What it trains: Summing up under time pressure, which is the core of chart insights and recommendations.

Structure recall (thinking)

Read one of the core frameworks, close it, redraw it from memory, check the gaps.

How much: 1-2 daily. What it trains: Recalling structures under stress.

Speed maths (thinking)

The Case maths drill on this site: percentages, big multiplications, breakevens. Accuracy first, then speed.

How much: 10 min daily. What it trains: Faster arithmetic leaves more attention for thinking.

Articulation (voice)

2-3 tongue twisters: slow and exaggerated, then at speed.

How much: 3 min pre-mock. What it trains: Crisp diction, so every number you say is heard clearly.

Paced reading (voice)

Read a business article aloud, slightly slower than feels natural, honouring every full stop.

How much: 5 min daily. What it trains: Controlling your pace. Measured speakers sound senior.

Pause practice (voice)

Record a 2-minute answer. Count the ums. Re-record with a silent pause where each filler was.

How much: 1 answer daily. What it trains: Replacing filler words with pauses.

Explain to the CEO (voice)

Explain any formula or framework aloud in 60 seconds to an imaginary busy executive.

How much: 1-2 daily. What it trains: Top-down, jargon-free delivery.

Read & listen (business language)

15 min of a strategy book, business press or a CEO interview. Note one story and one phrase.

How much: Daily. What it trains: Business vocabulary and real examples to use in cases.

Breathe (calm)

10 min breath-focused practice daily; box breathing 4-4-4-4 before every mock and interview.

How much: 10 min daily. What it trains: A calmer baseline and faster recovery when a case goes wrong.
outro: Read it once, then try it on a practice case today while it is fresh. One real attempt teaches more than three re-reads.
